0.0.n: With rising intonation, this sound expresses puzzlement or noticing something.

1.0.n: This borrowed noun names the thing that feels unusual.

1.1.n: が marks ポケット as the thing being described as strange.

1.2.n: Here, なんか makes the description vague: the speaker cannot quite identify what feels wrong.

1.3.n: 変 describes something unusual or not quite right.

1.4.n: です makes the description polite.

2.0.n: Said with rising intonation, え expresses surprise or confusion.

3.0.n: Japanese nouns do not mark singular or plural, so context tells us how many gloves there are.

3.1.n: が identifies 手袋 as what came out.

3.2.n: 出る becomes 出て, followed by きました, the polite past of 来る, suggesting movement out toward the speaker.

4.0.n: The speaker uses this noun to identify the items just discovered.

4.1.n: です politely identifies the items; Japanese leaves out the understood subject here.

5.0.n: This borrowed color noun describes the gloves through の.

5.1.n: の links the color noun グレー to 手袋, showing what color the gloves are.

5.2.n: グレーの comes before this noun to describe its color.

5.3.n: です politely finishes the identification without repeating the understood subject.

6.0.n: 右 means right, and 手 means hand.

6.1.n: に marks the hand where the glove is placed.

6.2.n: Here, the right-hand context indicates one glove, although the noun itself does not specify number.

6.3.n: を marks 手袋 as the item being put on.

6.4.n: します is the polite form of する; with 手袋, it means putting on or wearing gloves.

7.0.n: 左 means left, contrasting this hand with the right hand in the previous line.

7.1.n: に again marks the hand receiving the glove.

7.2.n: も follows に to add the left hand as another place to put a glove.

7.3.n: The polite form します repeats the previous action, with 手袋を left out because it is understood.

8.0.n: This exclamation expresses a comfortable, relieved reaction here.

8.2.n: あったかい is a casual spoken version of 暖かい, used here to express how pleasantly warm the hands feel.

0.tip: Rising intonation turns ん into a brief expression of puzzlement.

1.tip: なんか before a description means something like somehow or kind of, rather than naming a specific thing.

2.tip: え？ is a common short reaction to something unexpected.

3.tip: 出てくる describes something coming out toward the speaker or into view.

4.tip: Japanese often leaves out the subject when it is clear from context.

5.tip: A color noun such as グレー uses の before the thing it describes.

6.lit: On the right hand, [I] put on a glove.
6.tip: 手袋をする is a standard way to say put on or wear gloves.

7.lit: On the left hand too, [I] put [one] on.
7.tip: にも combines the location marked by に with the added sense of too from も.

8.tip: In casual speech, 暖かい often becomes あったかい.
